app: sast-engine/benchmarks/lashop/overlay on a fresh `composer create-project laravel/framework:^11.0` (Laravel v11.57.1), 111 locked packages (65 MB vendor, 7,650 PHP files). Rebuilt by sca/benchmarks/holdouts/build-lashop.sh; not committed.
note: Written before the analysis was first run on this app, after reading the app's own code. `truth` is what a person reading the code and the framework's config can establish. `expected` is what a sound static analysis should report given its stated limits: Laravel reaches app code through the framework (routing, the service container, facades, string-keyed validation rules), which a static call graph can't follow, so Unknown is the honest answer for every row. A Reachable here would be a false Reachable; Present-only would be an unsafe reassurance, since the app plainly uses laravel/framework.

rows.evidence: CRLF injection in the default `email` validation rule. The app's only validate() call (ApiController.php:23) uses 'required|string'; `email` is never a rule it uses (it appears only as a model attribute in User.php). The OSV record lists no fix commit and no function.

Temporary signed URL path confusion. The app never makes a signed URL (no signedRoute/temporarySignedRoute) and no route uses the `signed` middleware or ValidateSignature. No fix commit and no function in the record.

TokenGuard authentication bypass. config/auth.php defines only the `web` session guard; nothing in the app, its routes or its config uses a token driver, `auth:api` or TokenGuard, and the shop has no authentication at all.

XSS in the debug page. It only applies when APP_DEBUG is true. The source ships .env.example with APP_DEBUG=true; the container build flips it to false. Which one runs depends on the deployment, so it can't be settled from the code: any reassuring status would be unsafe.
